sanskrit: kaumārād yauvanaṃ cāpi sthāviryaṃ cāpi yauvanāt anena kramayogena pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ na labhyate
english: From childhood comes youth, and from youth comes old age; by this sequence of stages the earlier condition can never be regained.

sanskrit: kalānāṃ pṛthagarthānāṃ pratibhedaḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe vartate sarvabhūteṣu saukṣmyāt tu na vibhāvyate
english: The transformation of the constituent parts, each with its own function, proceeds moment by moment in all beings; but because it is so subtle it is not perceived.

sanskrit: na caiṣām apyayo rājaṃl lakṣyate prabhavo na ca avasthāyām avasthāyāṃ dīpasyevārciṣo gatiḥ
english: Neither their passing away nor their arising can be marked, O king, from one state to the next—it is like the motion of a lamp's flame.

sanskrit: tasyāpy evaṃprabhāvasya sadaśvasyeva dhāvataḥ ajasraṃ sarvalokasya kaḥ kuto vā na vā kutaḥ
english: And of this whole world, possessed of such power and ceaselessly running like a fine horse, who is it, and whence, or who is not, and from where?

sanskrit: kasyedaṃ kasya vā nedaṃ kuto vedaṃ na vā kutaḥ saṃbandhaḥ ko 'sti bhūtānāṃ svair apy avayavair iha
english: Whose is this, or whose is it not, whence is this, or whence is it not? What connection have living beings here even with their own bodily parts?

sanskrit: yathādityān maṇeś caiva vīrudbhyaś caiva pāvakaḥ bhavaty evaṃ samudayāt kalānām api jantavaḥ
english: As fire arises from the sun, from the crystal, and from kindling-plants, so too do living creatures arise from the assemblage of constituent parts.

sanskrit: ātmany evātmanātmānaṃ yathā tvam anupaśyasi evam evātmanātmānam anyasmin kiṃ na paśyasi yady ātmani parasmiṃś ca samatām adhyavasyasi
english: Just as you behold the self in the self by the self, why do you not likewise behold the self by the self in another—if you hold to the sameness of the self in yourself and in another?

sanskrit: atha māṃ kāsi kasyeti kimartham anupṛcchasi idaṃ me syād idaṃ neti dvaṃdvair muktasya maithila kāsi kasya kuto veti vacane kiṃ prayojanam
english: Then why do you keep asking me, 'Who are you, whose are you?' For one freed from the pairs of opposites—'this is mine, this is not'—O king of Mithilā, what purpose has the question, 'Who are you, whose, and whence?'

sanskrit: ripau mitre 'tha madhyasthe vijaye saṃdhivigrahe kṛtavān yo mahīpāla kiṃ tasmin muktalakṣaṇam
english: In one who still acts toward foe, friend, and the neutral party, toward conquest, peace, and war, O ruler of the earth—what mark of the liberated is there in him?

sanskrit: trivarge saptadhā vyaktaṃ yo na vedeha karmasu saṅgavān yas trivarge ca kiṃ tasmin muktalakṣaṇam
english: In one who does not clearly know the sevenfold division within the threefold aim amid his deeds, and who is still attached to that triad of aims—what mark of the liberated is there in him?

sanskrit: priye caivāpriye caiva durbale balavaty api yasya nāsti samaṃ cakṣuḥ kiṃ tasmin muktalakṣaṇam
english: In one whose eye is not equal toward the pleasant and the unpleasant, toward the weak and the strong—what mark of the liberated is there in him?

sanskrit: tad amuktasya te mokṣe yo 'bhimāno bhaven nṛpa suhṛdbhiḥ sa nivāryas te vicittasyeva bheṣajaiḥ
english: Therefore, O king, that conceit of yours regarding liberation, while you are yet unliberated, ought to be checked by your friends, as a madman's delusion is checked by remedies.

sanskrit: tāni tāny anusaṃdṛśya saṅgasthānāny ariṃdama ātmanātmani saṃpaśyet kiṃ tasmin muktalakṣaṇam
english: Reviewing one by one these many seats of attachment, O subduer of foes, one should examine the self within the self—what mark of the liberated is there in him?

sanskrit: imāny anyāni sūkṣmāṇi mokṣam āśritya kāni cit caturaṅgapravṛttāni saṅgasthānāni me śṛṇu
english: Hear from me these and certain other subtle seats of attachment, bearing on liberation, that pertain to the fourfold array of kingship.

sanskrit: ya imāṃ pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnām ekacchatrāṃ praśāsti ha ekam eva sa vai rājā puram adhyāvasaty uta
english: He who rules this whole earth beneath a single parasol—that one king, after all, dwells in but a single city.

sanskrit: tatpure caikam evāsya gṛhaṃ yad adhitiṣṭhati gṛhe śayanam apy ekaṃ niśāyāṃ yatra līyate
english: And in that city he occupies but a single house; in that house but a single bed, where at night he sinks to rest.

sanskrit: śayyārdhaṃ tasya cāpy atra strīpūrvam adhitiṣṭhati tad anena prasaṅgena phalenaiveha yujyate
english: And of that bed too only half is his, the other side first taken by a woman; thus, by this reasoning, he is joined here only to that much fruit.

sanskrit: evam evopabhogeṣu bhojanācchādaneṣu ca guṇeṣu parimeyeṣu nigrahānugrahau prati
english: Just so it is with his enjoyments, with his food and clothing, with his measurable pleasures, and with regard to punishment and favor.

sanskrit: paratantraḥ sadā rājā svalpe so 'pi prasajjate saṃdhivigrahayoge ca kuto rājñaḥ svatantratā
english: The king is ever dependent on others; even in trifling matters he is entangled. In the affairs of peace and war, where then is the king's independence?

sanskrit: strīṣu krīḍāvihāreṣu nityam asyāsvatantratā mantre cāmātyasamitau kuta eva svatantratā
english: In matters of women, sport, and recreation his lack of freedom is constant; and in counsel and in the assembly of ministers, where then is there independence?

sanskrit: yadā tv ājñāpayaty anyāṃs tadāsyoktā svatantratā avaśaḥ kāryate tatra tasmiṃs tasmin guṇe sthitaḥ
english: It is only when he commands others that he is called independent; yet there too he is made to act against his will, bound to each particular obligation.

sanskrit: svaptukāmo na labhate svaptuṃ kāryārthibhir janaiḥ śayane cāpy anujñātaḥ supta utthāpyate 'vaśaḥ
english: Wishing to sleep, he is not allowed to sleep by people seeking his judgment on their affairs; even when granted leave to lie down and asleep, he is roused up against his will.

sanskrit: snāhy ālabha piba prāśa juhudhy agnīn yajeti ca vadasva śṛṇu cāpīti vivaśaḥ kāryate paraiḥ
english: 'Bathe! Touch this in consecration! Drink! Eat! Pour the oblations into the fires! Sacrifice! Speak! And listen!'—thus is he made to act, powerless, by others.

sanskrit: abhigamyābhigamyainaṃ yācante satataṃ narāḥ na cāpy utsahate dātuṃ vittarakṣī mahājanāt
english: Coming to him again and again, people constantly beg of him; yet, guarding his wealth, he cannot bring himself to give freely, fearing the multitude.

sanskrit: dāne kośakṣayo hy asya vairaṃ cāpy aprayacchataḥ kṣaṇenāsyopavartante doṣā vairāgyakārakāḥ
english: For in giving there is loss to his treasury, and in withholding there is enmity; in a moment there crowd upon him faults that breed disaffection.

sanskrit: prājñāñ śūrāṃs tathaivāḍhyān ekasthāne 'pi śaṅkate bhayam apy abhaye rājño yaiś ca nityam upāsyate
english: The wise, the brave, and the wealthy—even gathered in one place—he distrusts; even in safety the king feels fear of the very men by whom he is constantly attended.

sanskrit: yadā caite praduṣyanti rājan ye kīrtitā mayā tadaivāsya bhayaṃ tebhyo jāyate paśya yādṛśam
english: And when those whom I have named turn corrupt, O king, then fear of them is born in him—behold of what kind it is.

sanskrit: sarvaḥ sve sve gṛhe rājā sarvaḥ sve sve gṛhe gṛhī nigrahānugrahau kurvaṃs tulyo janaka rājabhiḥ
english: Every man is a king in his own house, every man a householder in his own house; in dealing out punishment and favor he is the equal of kings, O Janaka.

sanskrit: putrā dārās tathaivātmā kośo mitrāṇi saṃcayaḥ paraiḥ sādhāraṇā hy ete tais tair evāsya hetubhiḥ
english: Sons, wife, and even his own self, treasury, friends, and his stores—all these he shares in common with others, through this cause or that.

sanskrit: hato deśaḥ puraṃ dagdhaṃ pradhānaḥ kuñjaro mṛtaḥ lokasādhāraṇeṣv eṣu mithyājñānena tapyate
english: 'The land is ravaged, the city burned, the chief elephant is dead'—over these things, which he holds in common with all the world, he grieves through false understanding.

sanskrit: amukto mānasair duḥkhair icchādveṣapriyodbhavaiḥ śirorogādibhī rogais tathaiva vinipātibhiḥ
english: Unliberated, he is afflicted by mental sorrows born of desire, hatred, and affection, and likewise by diseases such as headache and the rest that strike him down.

sanskrit: dvaṃdvais tais tair upahataḥ sarvataḥ pariśaṅkitaḥ bahupratyarthikaṃ rājyam upāste gaṇayan niśāḥ
english: Smitten by these various pairs of opposites, suspicious on every side, he tends a kingdom beset with many adversaries, counting out the nights.

sanskrit: tad alpasukham atyarthaṃ bahuduḥkham asāravat ko rājyam abhipadyeta prāpya copaśamaṃ labhet
english: Who would take up a kingship of such scant happiness, exceeding sorrow, and no substance—and, having gained it, find peace thereby?

sanskrit: mamedam iti yac cedaṃ puraṃ rāṣṭraṃ ca manyase balaṃ kośam amātyāṃś ca kasyaitāni na vā nṛpa
english: This city and realm that you think 'this is mine,' this army, treasury, and ministers—whose are they, or are they no one's, O king?

sanskrit: mitrāmātyaṃ puraṃ rāṣṭraṃ daṇḍaḥ kośo mahīpatiḥ saptāṅgaś cakrasaṃghāto rājyam ity ucyate nṛpa
english: Allies and ministers, city and realm, the rod of punishment, treasury, and sovereign—this seven-limbed assemblage, this wheel, is what is called the kingdom, O king.

sanskrit: saptāṅgasyāsya rājyasya tridaṇḍasyeva tiṣṭhataḥ anyonyaguṇayuktasya kaḥ kena guṇato 'dhikaḥ
english: In this seven-limbed kingdom, standing firm like a tripod, its parts bound to one another in mutual benefit, which is superior to which in worth?

sanskrit: teṣu teṣu hi kāleṣu tat tad aṅgaṃ viśiṣyate yena yat sidhyate kāryaṃ tat prādhānyāya kalpate
english: For in each particular circumstance, this or that limb becomes preeminent; whichever accomplishes the task at hand is fit to be reckoned the foremost.

sanskrit: saptāṅgaś cāpi saṃghātas trayaś cānye nṛpottama saṃbhūya daśavargo 'yaṃ bhuṅkte rājyaṃ hi rājavat
english: The seven-limbed aggregate, with three others besides, O best of kings, together make this tenfold group, which enjoys the kingdom even as the king himself does.

sanskrit: yaś ca rājā mahotsāhaḥ kṣatradharmarato bhavet sa tuṣyed daśabhāgena tatas tv anyo daśāvaraiḥ
english: And the king who is of great energy and devoted to the duty of the warrior should be content with a tenth share; another, however, with less than a tenth.

sanskrit: nāsty asādhāraṇo rājā nāsti rājyam arājakam rājye 'sati kuto dharmo dharme 'sati kutaḥ param
english: There is no king who possesses anything not held in common, nor any kingdom without a king. Without a kingdom, whence dharma? Without dharma, whence the supreme goal?

sanskrit: yo 'py atra paramo dharmaḥ pavitraṃ rājarājyayoḥ pṛthivī dakṣiṇā yasya so 'śvamedho na vidyate
english: And even that supreme dharma which is the purifier of king and kingdom—the horse-sacrifice whose sacrificial fee is the whole earth—does not exist for me.

sanskrit: sāham etāni karmāṇi rājyaduḥkhāni maithila samarthā śataśo vaktum atha vāpi sahasraśaḥ
english: I am able, O king of Mithilā, to recount these deeds and the sorrows of kingship by the hundreds, or even by the thousands.

sanskrit: svadehe nābhiṣaṅgo me kutaḥ paraparigrahe na mām evaṃvidhāṃ muktām īdṛśaṃ vaktum arhasi
english: I have no clinging even to my own body; how then to another's possessions? You ought not to speak so to me, who am liberated in this way.

sanskrit: nanu nāma tvayā mokṣaḥ kṛtsnaḥ pañcaśikhāc chrutaḥ sopāyaḥ sopaniṣadaḥ sopāsaṅgaḥ saniścayaḥ
english: Surely you have heard the whole doctrine of liberation from Pañcaśikha—with its means, its esoteric teachings, its disciplines, and its settled conclusions.

sanskrit: tasya te muktasaṅgasya pāśān ākramya tiṣṭhataḥ chatrādiṣu viśeṣeṣu kathaṃ saṅgaḥ punar nṛpa
english: How then, O king, do you, who are free of attachment yet stand trampling upon its very bonds, have attachment once more to such distinctions as the royal parasol and the rest?

sanskrit: śrutaṃ te na śrutaṃ manye mithyā vāpi śrutaṃ śrutam atha vā śrutasaṃkāśaṃ śrutam anyac chrutaṃ tvayā
english: What you have heard, I think, you have not truly heard; or else what you heard you heard wrongly; or what merely resembled the teaching you heard; or you heard something else than the teaching.

sanskrit: athāpīmāsu saṃjñāsu laukikīṣu pratiṣṭhasi abhiṣaṅgāvarodhābhyāṃ baddhas tvaṃ prākṛto mayā
english: And if you still take your stand upon these worldly notions, then, bound by clinging and by restraint, you are judged by me to be but an ordinary man.

sanskrit: sattvenānupraveśo hi yo 'yaṃ tvayi kṛto mayā kiṃ tavāpakṛtaṃ tatra yadi mukto 'si sarvataḥ
english: As for this entering into you that I have effected by the power of mind—what harm has been done to you thereby, if you are indeed liberated in every respect?

sanskrit: niyamo hy eṣa dharmeṣu yatīnāṃ śūnyavāsitā śūnyam āvāsayantyā ca mayā kiṃ kasya dūṣitam
english: For this is the rule among the disciplines of ascetics—that they should dwell as in a void; and by me, dwelling thus within a void, what has been defiled, and whose?

sanskrit: na pāṇibhyāṃ na bāhubhyāṃ pādorubhyāṃ na cānagha na gātrāvayavair anyaiḥ spṛśāmi tvā narādhipa
english: Not with hands, not with arms, not with feet or thighs, O sinless one, nor with any other limb of the body do I touch you, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: kule mahati jātena hrīmatā dīrghadarśinā naitat sadasi vaktavyaṃ sad vāsad vā mithaḥ kṛtam
english: By one born in a great family, possessed of modesty and far-sighted wisdom, what is done privately between two people, whether proper or improper, ought not to be spoken of in the assembly.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā guravaś ceme tathāmātyā gurūttamāḥ tvaṃ cātha gurur apy eṣām evam anyonyagauravam
english: These Brāhmaṇas are venerable, and these ministers most worthy of honor; and you, moreover, are venerable even to them—thus there is mutual reverence among you.

sanskrit: tad evam anusaṃdṛśya vācyāvācyaṃ parīkṣatā strīpuṃsoḥ samavāyo 'yaṃ tvayā vācyo na saṃsadi
english: Therefore, reflecting in this way and examining what should and should not be said, you ought not to speak of this meeting of a woman and a man in the assembly.

sanskrit: yathā puṣkaraparṇasthaṃ jalaṃ tatparṇasaṃsthitam tiṣṭhaty aspṛśatī tadvat tvayi vatsyāmi maithila
english: As water resting on a lotus-leaf abides upon that leaf without touching it, so shall I dwell within you, O king of Mithilā.

sanskrit: yadi vāpy aspṛśantyā me sparśaṃ jānāsi kaṃ cana jñānaṃ kṛtam abījaṃ te kathaṃ teneha bhikṣuṇā
english: And if you fancy any contact in me, who touch nothing at all, then how, by this mendicant woman, has your seedless knowledge been rendered fruitful here?

sanskrit: sa gārhasthyāc cyutaś ca tvaṃ mokṣaṃ nāvāpya durvidam ubhayor antarāle ca vartase mokṣavātikaḥ
english: Fallen from the householder's life, yet not having attained that liberation so hard to know, you remain in the middle between the two, a mere pretender to release.

sanskrit: na hi muktasya muktena jñasyaikatvapṛthaktvayoḥ bhāvābhāvasamāyoge jāyate varṇasaṃkaraḥ
english: For between one liberated and a liberated knower, in the matter of oneness and separateness, in the conjunction of being and non-being, no confusion of classes can arise.

sanskrit: varṇāśramapṛthaktve ca dṛṣṭārthasyāpṛthaktvinaḥ nānyad anyad iti jñātvā nānyad anyat pravartate
english: And though the classes and orders be distinct, for one who has seen the truth and is himself undivided, knowing that the one is not the other, the one does not pass over into the other.

sanskrit: pāṇau kuṇḍaṃ tathā kuṇḍe payaḥ payasi makṣikāḥ āśritāśrayayogena pṛthaktvenāśrayā vayam
english: The bowl in the hand, the milk in the bowl, the flies in the milk—by the relation of the supported to its support, we abide each one separately upon our support.

sanskrit: na tu kuṇḍe payobhāvaḥ payaś cāpi na makṣikāḥ svayam evāśrayanty ete bhāvā na tu parāśrayam
english: But the milk has no part in the nature of the bowl, nor the flies in the milk; these things rest each upon its own support, not by merging with another.

sanskrit: pṛthaktvād āśramāṇāṃ ca varṇānyatve tathaiva ca parasparapṛthaktvāc ca kathaṃ te varṇasaṃkaraḥ
english: Since the orders of life are distinct, and the classes likewise are diverse, and since all stand separate from one another, how can there be any confusion of classes for you?

sanskrit: nāsmi varṇottamā jātyā na vaiśyā nāvarā tathā tava rājan savarṇāsmi śuddhayonir aviplutā
english: I am not of the highest class by birth, nor a Vaiśyā, nor of a lower order; I am, O king, of your own class, of pure lineage and unsullied.

sanskrit: pradhāno nāma rājarṣir vyaktaṃ te śrotram āgataḥ kule tasya samutpannāṃ sulabhāṃ nāma viddhi mām
english: There was a royal sage named Pradhāna—surely his name has reached your ears; know me to be born in his line, Sulabhā by name.

sanskrit: droṇaś ca śataśṛṅgaś ca vakradvāraś ca parvataḥ mama satreṣu pūrveṣāṃ citā maghavatā saha
english: Droṇa, Śataśṛṅga, and the mountain Vakradvāra—these were heaped up at the sacrifices of my forebears, together with Maghavat.

sanskrit: sāhaṃ tasmin kule jātā bhartary asati madvidhe vinītā mokṣadharmeṣu carāmy ekā munivratam
english: Born in that lineage, and finding no husband fit for one like me, schooled in the disciplines of liberation, I wander alone, keeping the vow of a sage.

sanskrit: nāsmi satrapraticchannā na parasvābhimāninī na dharmasaṃkarakarī svadharme 'smi dhṛtavratā
english: I am no one concealed under a deceitful guise, nor one who lays false claim to others' goods, nor one who causes confusion of dharma; I am steadfast in my vow within my own dharma.

sanskrit: nāsthirā svapratijñāyāṃ nāsamīkṣyapravādinī nāsamīkṣyāgatā cāhaṃ tvatsakāśaṃ janādhipa
english: I am not unsteady in my own resolve, nor one who speaks without consideration; nor have I come into your presence, O ruler of men, without due reflection.

sanskrit: mokṣe te bhāvitāṃ buddhiṃ śrutvāhaṃ kuśalaiṣiṇī tava mokṣasya cāpy asya jijñāsārtham ihāgatā
english: Having heard that your mind was set upon liberation, and wishing you well, I have come here desiring to know the truth of this liberation of yours.

sanskrit: na vargasthā bravīmy etat svapakṣaparapakṣayoḥ mukto na mucyate yaś ca śānto yaś ca na śāmyati
english: I do not say this as a partisan of either side, my own or another's: whether one is liberated or not liberated, whether one is at peace or not at peace.

sanskrit: yathā śūnye purāgāre bhikṣur ekāṃ niśāṃ vaset tathā hi tvaccharīre 'sminn imāṃ vatsyāmi śarvarīm
english: As a mendicant might lodge a single night in an empty house in the city, so shall I dwell this one night within this body of yours.

sanskrit: sāham āsanadānena vāgātithyena cārcitā suptā suśaraṇā prītā śvo gamiṣyāmi maithila
english: Honored thus with the gift of a seat and the hospitality of speech, having slept well sheltered and content, tomorrow I shall depart, O king of Mithilā.

sanskrit: ity etāni sa vākyāni hetumanty arthavanti ca śrutvā nādhijagau rājā kiṃ cid anyad ataḥ param
english: Having heard these words, well-reasoned and full of meaning, the king could find nothing further to say in answer beyond this.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ nirvedam āpannaḥ śuko vaiyāsakiḥ purā etad icchāmi kauravya śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How did Śuka, the son of Vyāsa, come of old to detachment from the world? This I wish to hear, O Kaurava, for great is my curiosity.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca prākṛtena suvṛttena carantam akutobhayam adhyāpya kṛtsnaṃ svādhyāyam anvaśād vai pitā sutam
english: Bhīṣma said: When his son, of fair conduct and fearing nothing, was going his natural way, the father, having taught him the whole of sacred study, instructed him thus.

sanskrit: dharmaṃ putra niṣevasva sutīkṣṇau hi himātapau kṣutpipāse ca vāyuṃ ca jaya nityaṃ jitendriyaḥ
english: Cleave to dharma, my son, for sharp indeed are cold and heat; conquer hunger and thirst and the wind, ever having mastered your senses.

sanskrit: satyam ārjavam akrodham anasūyāṃ damaṃ tapaḥ ahiṃsāṃ cānṛśaṃsyaṃ ca vidhivat paripālaya
english: Truth, uprightness, freedom from anger, freedom from envy, self-restraint, austerity, non-injury, and gentleness—observe these duly.

sanskrit: satye tiṣṭha rato dharme hitvā sarvam anārjavam devatātithiśeṣeṇa yātrāṃ prāṇasya saṃśraya
english: Stand fast in truth, delighting in dharma, casting off all crookedness; sustain the journey of your life on what remains after the gods and guests are served.

sanskrit: phenapātropame dehe jīve śakunivat sthite anitye priyasaṃvāse kathaṃ svapiṣi putraka
english: While the body is like a vessel of foam and the soul perches in it like a bird, and the company of loved ones is impermanent—how can you sleep, my child?

sanskrit: apramatteṣu jāgratsu nityayukteṣu śatruṣu antaraṃ lipsamāneṣu bālas tvaṃ nāvabudhyase
english: While the foes are watchful, awake, ever intent, and seeking an opening, you, in your childishness, do not awaken to it.

sanskrit: gaṇyamāneṣu varṣeṣu kṣīyamāṇe tathāyuṣi jīvite śiṣyamāṇe ca kim utthāya na dhāvasi
english: As the years are being counted off, as your life-span dwindles and the time left to live grows ever less, why do you not rise up and run?
